explanations.Erdos9796Mission.problem97: Assume for contradiction that a nonempty convex-independent finite set A has four equidistant neighbours at every vertex. Strong induction on |A| rules this out. The counting child gives 9 ≤ |A|. If |A| = 9, finite_nine_exclusion is the contradiction. If 9 < |A|, the strong-induction hypothesis says that every smaller convex-independent K4 set is impossible. Passing that minimality hypothesis to minimal_counterexample_removable produces x ∈ A for which A.erase x still has the K4 property. Erasure strictly lowers cardinality, preserves nonemptiness because |A| > 9, and preserves convex independence by convex-hull monotonicity, so the induction hypothesis gives the contradiction. The counting child's geometric route follows Dumitrescu (2006), with cap-witness refinements attributed to Nivasch–Pach–Pinchasi–Zerbib (2013). This strong-induction assembly is this project's Lean reduction; the citations record the provenance of its counting input rather than attributing the whole reduction to either paper.
explanations.Erdos9796Mission.problem96: Import the proved bridge linear_bound_of_problem97 and supply the imported Problem 97 theorem as its hypothesis. The bridge's first conclusion is the explicit per-set inequality u(A) ≤ 3|A|, obtained by repeatedly deleting a vertex with at most three unit-distance neighbours and charging each pair when its first endpoint is deleted. Its second conclusion is exactly the mission's Problem 96 statement, U_c(n) = O(n), so projecting that component closes this target while recording both problem97 and the bridge as graph dependencies.
explanations.Erdos9796Mission.combined: The mission root is a conjunction. The two imported headline theorems supply its left and right components directly: problem97 proves the equidistant-neighbour statement, and problem96 proves the linear unit-distance bound. Constructing the pair records both branches as children of the mission root and makes the displayed graph reflect why the two Erdős problems were packaged together.
